R and Stata side by side

Source: vignettes/articles/r-and-stata.Rmd
r-and-stata.Rmd

The R package and the Stata command implement the same calculations. The Stata command is a port of R package version 0.3.0.

Commands

What R Stata
Calibrate the level alphaN(n, BF) alphan n, bf()
Power at the calibrated level alphaN_power(n, d, BF) alphan power n, d() bf()
Settings report alphaN_report(n, BF) alphan report n, bf()
Bayes factors after a fit JAB(model, covariate) alphan jab [coefficients]
Bayes factor from a t statistic JABt(n, t) alphan jabt t, n()
Bayes factor from a p-value JABp(n, p, z, df) alphan jabp p, n() [df()]
Klauer Bayes factor klauerBF(n, t, Fstat) alphan klauerbf, n() t() fstat()
Effective sample size n_effective(n, se, se_robust) alphan n_effective, n() se() se_robust()
Level against sample size alphaN_plot(BF) alphan plot, bf()
Power against sample size alphaN_power_plot(d, BF) alphan powerplot, d() bf()
Bayes factor against p-value JAB_plot(n, BF) alphan jabplot n, bf()

Arguments and options

R argument Stata option Meaning
BF bf() Target Bayes factor
method method() "JAB", "min", "robust", "balanced", "ES", "moment"; in Stata, case does not matter
upper upper() Upper limit of realistic effects (balanced)
de de() Targeted effect size (ES, moment)
nu nu() Degrees of freedom of the prior (ES, moment)
r r() Scale of the prior (ES)
q q() Coefficients tested jointly (ES, moment)
p p() Parameters retained under the null (ES, moment)
d d() Standardized effect for power
power_at powerat() Effects for the power section of the report
file saving(filename [, replace]) Where to write the report
width width() Line width of the report
methods, max, ylim, log, ref methods(), max(), ylim(), log(), ref() Graph settings; noref in Stata corresponds to ref = NULL

Numeric lists are recycled in Stata as vectors are in R.

Things that differ by design

  • alphan jab reads e(b), e(V) and e(N), so it runs after any Stata estimator and uses that estimator’s standard errors. JAB() accepts lm and glm objects and uses their classical standard errors; for cluster-robust ones, pass the statistics to JABt(), as in the worked example.
  • alphan jab takes an n() option, for instance to use an effective sample size. In R, the same is JABt(ne, t).
  • Bayes factors too large for a double are Inf in R and about 8e+307 in Stata.
  • Stata prints a table and leaves the numbers in r(), including r(table) with one row per case.
  • The graphs have the same colors and contents, but a different layout engine.

How closely they agree

tests/run-tests.do in the Stata repository compares the command with more than 1,100 reference values written by the R package. The checks enforce these tolerances:

Quantity Relative tolerance
Level, JAB, min and robust 1e-12
Level, balanced 1e-8
Level, ES and moment, up to n = 10,000 2e-5
Level, ES and moment, all n up to 100,000 1e-3
Bayes factors from t (n up to 1,000) and from F (BF above 1e-4) 2e-5
Bayes factors from t and F, the rest, down to BF of 1e-12 2e-3
Power 2e-5
JAB() after lm() and regress 1e-9
JAB() after glm() and logit, which stop iterating at different points 1e-5

The tests also reproduce the Bayes factors printed in Tables 7 and 8 of Klauer et al. (2025) and compare the text of the settings report line by line.

The largest gaps come from the R side. R package 0.3.0 integrates the balanced method numerically where the Stata command uses the closed form of the integral; the next R release uses the closed form too. For very small Bayes factors at a sample size of 60,000, a 40-digit evaluation agrees with Stata and not with R, whose integration tolerance is coarser. Over the range tested (sample sizes up to 2.5 million, upper of at most 1) the gaps are far too small to matter for any decision about a significance level.

Version

This page describes R package 0.3.0 and Stata command 0.3.0. The command is written for Stata 14 or later and has been tested on StataNow 19.5.
